chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Ḥakam al-Aʿmā and Hishām ibn Sālim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

A man said to another man, “O son of the fornicatress,” meaning zinā. He عليه السلام said: “If his mother is alive and present, then she comes and demands her right, he is to be struck with eighty lashes. If she is absent, it is to be awaited for her until she arrives and demands her right. If she has died, and nothing is known of her except good, the slanderer against her is to be given the hadd of eighty lashes.”

key_terms.اَلزِّنَى: zinā, illicit sexual intercourse intended here as the content of the accusation
key_terms.اَلْمُفْتَرِي: the slanderer, the one who fabricates a false accusation
key_terms.تَطْلُبُ حَقَّهَا: she demands her legal right arising from the slander against her
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً: eighty lashes, the hadd penalty mentioned in this case
key_terms.حَيَّةً شَاهِدَةً: alive and present to pursue the claim
key_terms.غَائِبَةً: absent, such that enforcement awaits her arrival
key_terms.لَمْ يُعْلَمْ مِنْهَا إِلَّا خَيْرًا: nothing was known of her except goodness, establishing her upright reputation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone says to another person, “O son of a fornicatress”?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning false accusation and insulting a person through imputing zinā to his mother. It explains when the hadd punishment is carried out, distinguishing between the mother being present, absent, or deceased with a known good reputation.
